groups.title: Inherently impersonal VNCs and fictitious subjects
groups.proposal: Recognize the exact inherently impersonal lexical stems, keep their grammatical subject fixed as third-person singular, and distinguish a fictitious subject from both a real referent and a missing subject.
groups.writingJob: Build an inherently impersonal VNC from any entered intransitive Source whose typed lexical analysis is selected, use known Canvas stems only as defaults and examples, force the empty third-person singular subject frame, and realize ordinary tense and sentence material without creating a personal subject.
groups.readingJob: Show that the VNC is agentless but not subjectless, identify the grammatical subject as a nonreferential fiction, and present the licensed meteorological or event reading without treating an English gloss as grammar.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the lexical stem and ordinary tense or mood. The application recognizes an inherently impersonal stem and fixes its subject automatically; there is no personal-versus-impersonal switch for a stem that can occur only impersonally.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse stem, tense, mood, polarity, and sentence controls; do not add fictitious-subject, third-person, agentless, meteorological, or supplementability switches.

groups.title: Nonanimate subjects are not impersonal subjects
groups.proposal: Keep a specific nonanimate common-number subject separate from a truly impersonal subject: both use third-person singular morphology, but only the nonanimate subject has an identifiable referent and can be supplemented.
groups.writingJob: Preserve the third-person singular surface shared by both constructions while using typed referent and supplementation structure to keep a nonanimate common-number subject personal and an empty impersonal subject unsupplementable.
groups.readingJob: Show whether the subject refers to one or more nameable nonanimate entities or to no entity at all, and explain why visible singular morphology does not erase common number or authorize an impersonal reading.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies an actual subject supplement or referential context when one is intended. The application combines that structure with lexical Source authority; merely omitting a visible supplement never turns an ordinary nonanimate subject into an impersonal one.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse subject supplement and referent cues; do not add singular-versus-common-number, nameability, supplementability, or nonanimate-versus-impersonal switches.

groups.title: Transform an active VNC into impersonal voice
groups.proposal: When impersonal voice is genuinely available, replace the active personal subject with a faceless third-person singular subject, derive the nonactive stem, allow intransitive or eligible transitive Sources, and reject a Source with a specific projective object while allowing reflexive or nonspecific objects.
groups.writingJob: Validate the active Source, discard its personal subject, import the fixed impersonal subject, derive the owner-issued nonactive stem, preserve eligible valence, and block specific projective-object Sources without confusing the result with passive voice.
groups.readingJob: Show the unrecoverable source subject, the faceless but existent general agent, the general or total human readings, and the exact difference from inherent impersonal and passive constructions.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses impersonal voice only when the active Source permits a genuine active, passive, or impersonal presentation choice. The application performs subject replacement, nonactive formation, and object-eligibility checks automatically.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse active Source, Voice, Valence, and object controls; do not add faceless-agent, replace-subject, derive-nonactive, generality, totality, or passive-versus-impersonal repair switches.

groups.title: Impersonal formula, intransitive Sources, and irregular Results
groups.proposal: Keep the active Source formula's valence, replace only its subject and stem authority, and generate ordinary and irregular impersonal Results through the canonical finite tense path.
groups.writingJob: Preserve intransitive or transitive formula shape, install the fixed impersonal subject, discard the source subject without a recoverable trace, and reuse owner-issued ordinary or suppletive nonactive stems in their licensed tense cells.
groups.readingJob: Show active and impersonal formulas side by side, preserve the full range of general-human readings, and explain inherited irregular tense and meaning dislocation.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses ordinary tense and sentence coordinates. Source valence, impersonal subject, nonactive stem, and any irregular cell are automatic consequences of the typed Source.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the familiar tense, mood, and output controls; do not add formula-shape, imported-subject, source-subject recovery, irregular-impersonal, or gloss switches.

groups.title: Retain nonspecific objects in impersonal voice
groups.proposal: Carry source tē and tla unchanged into the impersonal Result, including two-object Sources, while preserving the genuine generalized active and patient-oriented readings authorized by context.
groups.writingJob: Retain each nonspecific human or nonhuman object carrier and its typed role while replacing only the source subject and stem, then preserve every licensed reading without selecting a preferred English paraphrase.
groups.readingJob: Identify the general subject and each retained nonspecific object, and display the active-like, distributive, reciprocal-looking, or patient-focused readings as interpretations of one unchanged formula.
groups.decisionSplit: The typed Source determines which nonspecific objects survive. The user chooses a reading only where the unchanged grammar genuinely supports more than one intended interpretation.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source object and Reading controls conditionally; do not add retain-tē, retain-tla, generalized-subject, distributive, or patient-focus switches.

groups.title: Reflexive Sources become impersonal ne
groups.proposal: When the active Source has a reflexive object, replace the personal subject with the impersonal subject and realize the now-impersonalized reflexive relation automatically as shuntline ne, preserving any additional nonspecific object.
groups.writingJob: Convert the Source reflexive object to ne, retain other eligible object carriers, install the fixed impersonal subject, and derive the owner-issued nonactive stem without adding a new participant.
groups.readingJob: Trace the original subject and reflexive relation into the general-human impersonal reading, identify ne as the transformed reflexive carrier, and show any retained tla separately.
groups.decisionSplit: The user composes the reflexive Source and requests impersonal voice; ne and any retained nonspecific object are automatic. Reflexive versus reciprocal remains a choice only where the plural Source genuinely permits both.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse reflexive or reciprocal Source interpretation and impersonal Voice; do not add ne, retain-object, or impersonalize-reflexive controls.

groups.title: Impersonal wishes, commands, and admonitions
groups.proposal: Send a completed impersonal VNC through the ordinary optative and admonitive sentence paths while preserving impersonal subject and stem authority.
groups.writingJob: Keep the impersonal Result intact while applying the selected wish, command, exhortation, negative, past-optative, or admonitive sentence material.
groups.readingJob: Show the impersonal assertion inside the familiar sentence frame and explain the licensed force without inventing impersonal-specific mood grammar.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended sentence force; the application derives its compatible tense, negation, and introductory material around the completed impersonal Result.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse ordinary mood and sentence controls; do not add impersonal wish, command, exhortation, negative, or admonition controls.

groups.title: Derivational tla-impersonal stems
groups.proposal: Derive tla-impersonal stems productively from any entered typed intransitive Source, keep derivational tla inside the stem and distinct from object tla, and use Canvas-listed Sources only for known defaults, sound adjustments, and attested readings.
groups.writingJob: Validate the exact lexical Source, apply its owner-issued tla derivation and sound adjustment, build the fixed impersonal subject, and realize ordinary finite forms without accepting a caller-supplied target stem.
groups.readingJob: Show derivational tla inside the verbstem, distinguish it from nonspecific-object tla, trace attested or reconstructed Sources, and present the licensed general, meteorological, idiomatic, or rare animate reading.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses an intended lexical Source and ordinary finite coordinates. The application derives tla-impersonal only where Canvas licenses it; target shape, semantic class, and general subject are not free choices.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source, impersonal Voice, generated formation, tense, mood, and Reading controls conditionally; do not add prefix-kind, caller-entered target, meteorological, reconstructed, inherent-layer, or animate-generality switches.
